newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan nurses, doctors threaten to strike.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan nurses, doctors threaten to strike.

text.p: Doctors and nurses at Sri Lanka's government hospitals are threatening to strike next week to back demands for better pay and to protest against cuts in overtime payments.

Nurses' union head Muruththetuwe Ananda was quoted as saying on Sunday that its 14,000 members planned to stage an islandwide strike if the government failed to scrap the cuts in overtime payments by March 5.

"In the 585 state-run hospitals there is a shortage of nurses and as such working overtime is inevitable," Ananda, of the Public Services United Nurses' Union, told the state-run Sunday Observer newspaper.
Ananda was not immediately available for comment.
Government doctors, who staged a half-day strike last Thursday which severely disrupted services in about 700 hospitals, are threatening a token stoppage this week too.
They are campaigning for higher wages.
The government, in its 1997 budget announced last November, cut overtime payments for government workers to reduce public-sector spending.
